speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I notice you are presenting with both a psychiatric condition and a new movement disorder. To help me understand what is happening, can you tell me the specific symptoms you are experiencing and when they first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. Since you were started on risperidone two months ago for schizophrenia and have had no other major changes in your routine, have you noticed any stiffness, shaking, or repetitive movements since beginning the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for describing that restlessness, pacing, and leg crossing; these are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent initiation of risperidone, this is a highly suspected medication-induced side effect. To confirm the severity and rule out other causes, I will need to check your vital signs and review your blood work for electrolyte imbalances.

REQUEST TEST: Vitals, CBC, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel
REQUEST TEST: Risperidone_serum_level
REQUEST IMAGES: None requested at this time.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia secondary to Risperidone therapy
